reviewers.summary: The study applies Poisson regression to a local dataset but lacks critical diagnostic checks (overdispersion, zero-inflation, distributional assessment) and does not describe missing data handling or variable distributions. Inappropriate residual diagnostics (Shapiro-Wilk on raw residuals) are reported. These omissions undermine the reliability of the estimates and limit interpretation. Substantial revisions are needed to include proper diagnostics and transparent reporting.

findings.title: Overdispersion not assessed
findings.whyItMatters: Overdispersed count data lead to underestimated standard errors and inflated Type I error; rate ratios may be unreliable. Without checking, the Poisson model may be misspecified.
findings.actionableFix: Report residual deviance, Pearson chi-square, and perform a dispersion test. If overdispersed, consider quasi-Poisson or negative binomial regression.
findings.deterministicVerification: Check if (residual deviance / df) > 1 or perform formal overdispersion test.

findings.title: Complete-case analysis without description of missing data
findings.whyItMatters: Missing data that are non-random can bias estimates and reduce generalizability. The handling of missingness is unstated.
findings.actionableFix: Provide a flow chart of cohort construction, report amount and patterns of missingness, consider sensitivity analysis (e.g., multiple imputation).
findings.deterministicVerification: Review data preprocessing steps and compare complete-case vs. original sample descriptives.

findings.title: Inappropriate use of Shapiro-Wilk test on raw Poisson residuals
findings.whyItMatters: Raw residuals from Poisson are not normally distributed; normality testing is irrelevant and may mislead model assessment.
findings.actionableFix: Replace with appropriate GLM diagnostics: deviance residuals, Pearson residuals, QQ-plot of deviance residuals, and test for dispersion.
findings.deterministicVerification: Remove Shapiro-Wilk and produce deviance-based diagnostic plots.

findings.title: No descriptive statistics for outcome and predictors
findings.whyItMatters: Without summaries (count distribution, zeros, covariate ranges), it's impossible to judge whether Poisson assumptions hold or if covariates are properly scaled.
findings.actionableFix: Add a table with summary statistics, including min, max, mean, variance of count_events, frequency of zeros, and distributions of treatment, age, severity.
findings.deterministicVerification: Verify that the reported descriptives match the data used in the model.

findings.title: Linearity assumption for continuous covariates not assessed
findings.whyItMatters: Misspecifying the functional form of age or severity can bias effect estimates and reduce model fit.
findings.actionableFix: Examine partial residuals or include flexible terms (e.g., splines) and compare fit.
findings.deterministicVerification: Check for non-linearity via component-plus-residual plots.

findings.title: No diagnostic figures referenced in manuscript
findings.whyItMatters: Visual diagnostics are essential for evaluating model fit, outliers, and patterns; their absence hampers credibility.
findings.actionableFix: Include key diagnostic plots (residuals vs fitted, QQ-plot of deviance residuals) in the manuscript or supplementary materials.
findings.deterministicVerification: Ensure plots are correctly generated and match reported summaries.

findings.title: Rate ratios not directly presented in results section
findings.whyItMatters: Clinically interpretable rate ratios are omitted from the main text, making results harder to understand for broader audiences.
findings.actionableFix: Report rate ratios with 95% CIs alongside log estimates in the results table.
findings.deterministicVerification: Recalculate rate ratios from log estimates and verify CIs.

findings.title: Potential zero-inflation not considered
findings.whyItMatters: A high proportion of zero counts violates Poisson assumptions; ignoring zero-inflation can skew estimates.
findings.actionableFix: Report the percentage of zero counts and, if substantial, consider zero-inflated Poisson or negative binomial models.
findings.deterministicVerification: Compare observed zero proportion to expected under Poisson using a chi-square test.

missingEvidence: Detailed missing data description (original N, exclusion criteria, patterns)
Descriptive statistics for all variables (count distribution, covariate summaries)
Diagnostic plots (residuals, QQ-plot of deviance residuals)
Full stats-qa.json (truncated artifact prevents verification of all QA checks)

reviewers.summary: The study fails to assess overdispersion in Poisson regression, lacks essential descriptive and variable-definition details, and provides incomplete QA artifacts, undermining reproducibility and validity.

findings.title: No assessment of overdispersion in Poisson regression
findings.whyItMatters: Poisson regression assumes mean = variance. Overdispersion inflates type I error rates and invalidates standard errors and p-values. The residual SD of 1.07 may indicate overdispersion, but no formal test or alternative model (e.g., negative binomial) was considered.
findings.actionableFix: Report dispersion parameter (e.g., deviance/df), perform a likelihood ratio test for overdispersion, or fit a negative binomial model and compare AIC. If overdispersion is present, use robust standard errors or switch to an appropriate model.

findings.title: Missing variable definitions and descriptive statistics
findings.whyItMatters: Without clear definitions of variables (treatment coding, units of age and severity, distribution of count_events), readers cannot interpret the results or assess model appropriateness. No table of descriptive statistics (e.g., mean event count, proportion treated, summary of covariates) is provided.
findings.actionableFix: Provide a table with variable definitions, levels, and descriptive statistics (mean, SD, range, count for categorical). Include a histogram or table of the outcome distribution to show event counts.

findings.title: Incomplete QA artifacts prevent full verification
findings.whyItMatters: The stats-qa.json artifact is truncated in the supplied packet, and the figure-qa.json is empty. This prevents reviewers from confirming that all QA checks passed and that figures were adequately reviewed. Reproducibility claims rely on these checks.
findings.actionableFix: Provide complete, non-truncated QA artifacts and figure QA results. Ensure all checks are documented.

findings.title: No handling or reporting of missing data
findings.whyItMatters: The analysis uses complete-case (N=240) but does not report the number of records excluded due to missingness or assess whether missingness is associated with variables. This could introduce selection bias.
findings.actionableFix: Report the number of excluded records, compare characteristics of excluded vs. included subjects, and consider sensitivity analyses (e.g., multiple imputation) if missingness is substantial.

findings.title: Inappropriate Shapiro-Wilk test on residuals
findings.whyItMatters: Poisson regression does not assume normally distributed residuals. The Shapiro-Wilk p-value (0.00008) is reported but not meaningful; it may mislead readers into thinking model assumption failed.
findings.actionableFix: Remove the Shapiro-Wilk test result or replace with appropriate diagnostics (e.g., deviance goodness-of-fit, overdispersion test, residual plots).

findings.title: Abstract lacks numeric results
findings.whyItMatters: The abstract does not include key effect estimates, confidence intervals, or sample size; this hinders quick comprehension.
findings.actionableFix: Include the rate ratio, 95% CI, and p-value for treatment, and mention sample size and model variables in the abstract.

findings.title: Title is a question rather than declarative
findings.whyItMatters: The title 'How is treatment associated with count-event burden after adjustment?' is a question; standard reporting requires a declarative title summarizing the study.
findings.actionableFix: Use a declarative title, e.g., 'Association between treatment and count-event burden in a Poisson regression analysis of 240 observations'.

missingEvidence: Distribution of count_events and descriptive statistics
Number and characteristics of records excluded due to missingness
Overdispersion test results or negative binomial model fit
Complete QA artifacts (stats-qa.json full content, figure-qa.json content)
Details of study design (population, time frame, data source)

reviewPanel.nextAction: Adjudicate findings and route accepted repairs back into the pipeline.
